subject: mathematics
question_text: If a + b + c = 0, |a| = 3, |b| = 5 and |c| = 7, find the angle between a and b.

mark_split.label: Move c to the other side and take magnitudes
Find the angle from cos θ

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 8, book p.68. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Computed twice. Symbolically: c = −(a + b) gives |c|² = |a|² + |b|² + 2(a·b), so 49 = 9 + 25 + 2(a·b), a·b = 15/2, and cos θ = (15/2)/(3 × 5) = 1/2, θ = 60° = π/3. Checked a second way by direct arithmetic on concrete vectors: with a = (3, 0) and b at 60° to it, b = (2.5, 4.330127); then a + b = (5.5, 4.330127) and |a + b| = √(30.25 + 18.75) = √49 = 7, which is exactly |c|, so the 60° answer reproduces the given data. Note the angle asked for is between a and b themselves, not between a and the side of the triangle opposite them; the interior angle of the triangle formed by the three vectors placed head to tail is the supplement, 120°. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the four separate acts: isolating c, expanding the square, solving for the dot product, and converting it to an angle. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors carries a Section B slot on the paper and also appears in Section C. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would get the angle between a and b when the three vectors add to zero — name each move in order.

steps.label: Isolate c and take magnitudes
steps.margin_note: First mark. The angle wanted is between a and b, so put a and b together on one side and the known length |c| on the other.
steps.memory_tip: Move the vector you are NOT asked about to its own side of the equation.

recall.must_convey: That c = −(a + b), so |c| = |a + b| and therefore |c|² = |a + b|².
accept: move c to the other side so c is minus a plus b
the magnitude of c equals the magnitude of a plus b
square both sides to get mod c squared equals mod a plus b squared
c ni other side ki teeskunte c equals minus a plus b
keep a and b together because the angle is between them

steps.why: Only the lengths are known, and a length reaches the dot product through its square. Isolating c puts the pair a, b together, which is where the wanted angle lives.
common_mistakes: Writing c = a + b and losing the minus sign, though squaring hides it here.
Isolating a instead of c, which puts the wanted angle inside the wrong bracket.

steps.label: Expand |a + b|²
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The minus sign disappears on squaring, because |−v|² = |v|². Substitute the three given lengths at once.
steps.memory_tip: |a + b|² = |a|² + |b|² + 2(a·b) — the same shape as (x + y)².

accept: expand mod a plus b squared as mod a squared plus mod b squared plus twice a dot b
forty nine equals nine plus twenty five plus two a dot b
substitute three five and seven into the expansion
expand cheste forty nine equals nine plus twenty five plus two a dot b

steps.why: The dot product is the only place an angle can enter, and expanding the square of a sum is what introduces it. Nothing else in the question mentions direction.
common_mistakes: Writing |a + b|² = |a|² + |b|² and dropping the 2(a·b) term.
Squaring the lengths as 3 × 2 = 6 instead of 3² = 9.

steps.label: Solve for a·b
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Simple rearrangement. Keep 15/2 as a fraction — it cancels cleanly against 15 in the next step.
steps.memory_tip: Keep a·b as the fraction 15/2; it cancels against |a||b| = 15.

accept: two a dot b is fifteen so a dot b is fifteen by two
forty nine minus thirty four is fifteen
the dot product comes to seven point five
forty nine minus thirty four fifteen, a dot b fifteen by two
rearrange to find the dot product

steps.why: The dot product is the bridge between the lengths, which are given, and the angle, which is wanted. This step crosses that bridge halfway.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide by 2 and taking a·b as 15.
Subtracting in the wrong order and getting a negative value.

steps.label: Find the angle
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos θ = 1/2 gives an exact standard angle, so write 60° and not an inverse cosine. The angle asked for is between a and b, not the interior angle of the triangle they form.
steps.memory_tip: cos θ = 1/2 is a standard value: θ = 60°.
lines: Let θ be the angle between a and b.

recall.must_convey: That cos θ = (a·b)/(|a||b|) = 1/2, so the angle between a and b is 60°.
accept: cos theta is a dot b over the product of the lengths which is a half
cos theta equals one half so theta is sixty degrees
the angle between a and b is sixty degrees or pi by three
cos theta half vasthundi kabatti theta sixty degrees
divide the dot product by fifteen to get one half

steps.why: The definition a·b = |a||b| cos θ is the only formula that turns a dot product back into an angle, and here the value is one of the standard cosines, so an exact answer is available.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as Cos⁻¹(1/2) when the exact angle 60° is known.
Giving 120°, which is the interior angle of the triangle, not the angle between a and b.
